stories.headline: Anthropic says an unreleased Claude raised a Riemann zeta bound from 41.6% to 67.2%

key_facts.fact: Anthropic said on August 10 that an unreleased research version of Claude improved the longstanding unconditional lower bound for the fraction of Riemann zeta zeros on the critical line from 41.6% to 67.2%, while failing at the Riemann hypothesis itself
key_facts.excerpt: An unreleased research version of Claude has improved on a longstanding lower bound for the fraction of zeros of the Riemann zeta function that satisfy the Riemann hypothesis... increased this bound from 41.6% to 67.2%.

key_facts.fact: The result came out of two Claude Code sessions totaling 31 million output tokens after staff member Jarred Sumner, a non-mathematician, asked Claude to 'take a real stab' at the Riemann hypothesis
key_facts.excerpt: An unreleased research version of Claude found the new lower bound over two sessions in Claude Code, using a total of 31 million output tokens.

key_facts.fact: Claude first generated 650 ideas that failed, then spent about a day and a half coordinating roughly 60 subagents that ran about 2,400 shell commands, wrote hundreds of Python scripts and refereed each other's work
key_facts.excerpt: Initially, Claude generated and tried 650 ideas, none of which worked... it spent a day and a half coordinating about 60 Claude subagents... between them, they ran 2,400 shell commands and wrote hundreds of Python scripts.

key_facts.fact: Claude's subagents downloaded 54 arXiv papers to check the result was new, searched for counterexamples and re-proved the finding from scratch; Claude then recommended a human number theorist validate it
key_facts.excerpt: Claude tested its work by having various subagents review the proofs, search for counterexamples, download 54 papers from the arXiv to check that its finding hadn't already been made, and independently re-prove its finding from scratch.

key_facts.fact: The paper is authored by the model itself and states results of at least 67.250% of zeros being simple and on the critical line and at least 83.625% being distinct, accompanied by a Lean 4 formalisation
key_facts.excerpt: The author of this paper is a large language model developed by Anthropic... with an optimised test family the three constants become 0.6725, 0.6725, 0.83625... A Lean 4 formalisation of Theorems A–E accompanies the paper.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic mathematicians Levent Alpöge and Ralph Furman reviewed the argument and outside number theorists Brian Conrey and Dan Goldston examined the paper on short notice; it has not been through conventional peer review
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic mathematicians Levent Alpöge and Ralph Furman subsequently analyzed the argument and its relationship to previous research. Conrey and Goldston, experts in the area, also examined the paper on short notice.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic says it does not expect Claude's method to lead directly to a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, and 67.2% does not mean the remaining zeros lie off the line
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic said it does not expect Claude's method to lead directly to a proof of the Riemann hypothesis... It improves a mathematical guarantee: at least 67.2% of the relevant zeros satisfy the condition required by the hypothesis.

stories.headline: OpenAI ships GPT-5.6-Cyber, a model trained to refuse fewer hacking requests, behind a vetted tier

key_facts.fact: OpenAI announced on August 10 that it is splitting its Daybreak cybersecurity program into two access tiers: Daybreak Blue for frontier general-purpose models with defensive safeguards and Daybreak Red for purpose-trained cyber models
key_facts.excerpt: Daybreak Blue provides access to frontier general-purpose models, including GPT-5.6 Sol... Daybreak Red provides access to our purpose-trained cybersecurity models for authorized vulnerability research, exploit validation, and security testing.

key_facts.fact: GPT-5.6-Cyber, built on GPT-5.6 Sol and available through Daybreak Red, is trained to find zero-day vulnerabilities and develop exploit chains and to reduce refusals on higher-risk dual-use tasks
key_facts.excerpt: Built on GPT-5.6 Sol, it is trained to improve capabilities on several specialized cybersecurity tasks (e.g., finding zero-day vulnerabilities and developing exploit chains) and to reduce refusals for certain higher-risk, dual-use cyber tasks.

key_facts.fact: On OpenAI's internal Advanced Cybersecurity Completion Rate evaluation, GPT-5.6-Cyber answers 95.0% of exploit-chain, authentication-bypass and privilege-escalation requests, versus 57.3% for GPT-5.5-Cyber, 2.0% via Daybreak Blue and 1.5% for standard GPT-5.6 Sol
key_facts.excerpt: GPT‑5.6‑Cyber completes 95.0% of these requests, compared with just 1.5% for GPT‑5.6 Sol, and 2.0% when used with Daybreak Blue access... GPT‑5.5‑Cyber, which completes only 57.3% of requests.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says the model analyzed Chrome's V8 JavaScript engine and found two previously unknown vulnerabilities that can be chained to corrupt memory and bypass the V8 heap sandbox; Google patched them under CVE-2026-15903
key_facts.excerpt: the model analyzed V8, Chrome's JavaScript engine, and found two previously unknown vulnerabilities that can be chained together to corrupt memory and bypass the V8 heap sandbox. Google fixed the flaws after coordinated disclosure and assigned them the CVE-2026-15903 designation.

key_facts.fact: Access is gated by identity verification, monitoring, approved-use restrictions and legal attestations, and hardware security keys become mandatory for Daybreak accounts on September 1, 2026
key_facts.excerpt: Getting into either tier requires identity verification, account security measures, monitoring, and legal declarations. Hardware security keys become mandatory for all Daybreak accounts on September 1, 2026.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI rates both GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.6-Cyber as High for cybersecurity capability under its Preparedness Framework but below the Critical threshold, and says GPT-5.6-Cyber was not involved in the Hugging Face exploitation incident
key_facts.excerpt: we also evaluated its frontier cyber capabilities and determined that it similarly reaches the High threshold but not the Critical threshold... GPT‑5.6‑Cyber was not involved in exploiting Hugging Face, nor are any other models planned for an upcoming release.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI launched Daybreak in May, shortly after Anthropic launched its own cybersecurity coalition, Project Glasswing, and the expansion follows AI-model security incidents disclosed by OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta in recent weeks
key_facts.excerpt: Back in June, OpenAI first introduced Daybreak alongside GPT-5.5-Cyber, giving selected security researchers access to the stronger cyber capabilities of frontier models under additional safeguards.

stories.headline: Anthropic will watermark every Claude text output worldwide to comply with the EU AI Act

key_facts.fact: Anthropic said in a help document published Monday that generated text from new Claude models will carry embedded watermarks and generated files will include digitally signed provenance metadata, as part of complying with the EU AI Act's transparency rules
key_facts.excerpt: "Generated text will carry embedded watermarks, and generated files will include digitally signed provenance metadata where supported," the company said in a help document published on Monday.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic signed the EU AI Act's Article 50(2) Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content; Claude models launched on or after August 2, 2026 support machine-readable marking at launch, and earlier models are being retrofitted during the transition period
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has signed the EU AI Act Code of Practice on transparency for AI-generated content... Claude models that launch in the EU on or after August 2, 2026, will ship with this labeling baked in.

key_facts.fact: The marking applies globally rather than only in the EU, covering the Claude API, Claude, Claude Code, Claude Cowork and Claude Tag, plus Claude models served through AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry
key_facts.excerpt: "Marking will apply to output from supported models wherever Claude is offered, worldwide."... This also includes third-party providers of Anthropic models like AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry.

key_facts.fact: Text carries an imperceptible watermark woven into the text itself that travels with copy-paste and 'may persist through some editing'; supported files (.svg, .png, .jpg) get signed metadata following the C2PA standard
key_facts.excerpt: The watermark will also move with text even if it is copied, pasted elsewhere, and lightly edited. Anthropic further noted that when Claude generates a supported file type (.svg, .png, or .jpg), signed provenance metadata will be attached.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic concedes a detected mark is not conclusive evidence Claude wrote the content, since users also have Claude proofread or translate their own text, and that absence of a mark does not prove human authorship
key_facts.excerpt: a watermark doesn't prove Claude wrote the content, since people often use the AI to edit or translate their own text. Heavy editing or format changes can also strip the markings entirely.

key_facts.fact: The detection tool that would let third parties check for the mark has not yet shipped, and Anthropic has not published the watermarking algorithm or a false-positive rate
key_facts.excerpt: The detection tool that would let anyone check for the mark has not yet shipped.

key_facts.fact: EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations became applicable on August 2, 2026, requiring providers to mark generative AI outputs including text in a machine-readable format
key_facts.excerpt: These transparency obligations, applicable from 2 August 2026... Outputs of AI systems (audio, image, video, text) are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated.

stories.headline: Anthropic signs a $9.1B, 20-year compute lease with bitcoin miner Riot Platforms

key_facts.fact: Riot Platforms disclosed on August 10 a 20-year lease for 191 MW of data center capacity at its Rockdale, Texas campus with an unnamed 'leading frontier AI lab'; Bloomberg identified the customer as Anthropic
key_facts.excerpt: Riot disclosed the deal on Monday, describing the counterparty only as a "leading frontier AI lab." Riot's Rockdale, Texas, campus will supply 191 megawatts of IT capacity under the terms of the 20-year lease, which extends through June 2048.

key_facts.fact: The contract runs through June 2048 and is expected to generate $9.1 billion in revenue for Riot; two five-year extension options could raise the total to $16.1 billion
key_facts.excerpt: Riot confirmed the agreement in an August 10 statement, noting that it is entering a 20-year contract with Anthropic that will run through June 2048. The deal is expected to generate $9.1 billion in revenue for Riot over the initial term.

key_facts.fact: Capacity comes online in stages: 96 MW by December 2027 and the full 191 MW by June 2028; the 191 MW is roughly the power draw of about 143,000 homes
key_facts.excerpt: Under the agreement, Riot will provide 191 megawatts (MW) of data center capacity from its Rockdale campus in Texas. The capacity is roughly equivalent to the electricity used by about 143,000 homes at any given time.

key_facts.fact: Riot stock jumped more than 25% after hours on Monday and was up around 21% in premarket trading on Tuesday
key_facts.excerpt: Following the news, Riot's stock rose over 25% in after-hours trading. As of press time, Riot was up 21.29% in overnight trading.

key_facts.fact: Riot, a bitcoin miner that mined 1,587 bitcoin in the second quarter of 2026, has now signed 241 MW of data center leases worth about $9.8 billion in six months, the other tenant being AMD
key_facts.excerpt: Riot Platforms is a bitcoin miner by heritage... having mined 1,587 bitcoin in the second quarter of 2026 alone... "executed leases totaling 241 megawatts of capacity, representing approximately $9.8 billion of long-term, contracted revenue".

key_facts.fact: Riot arranged a $573 million interim financing facility through Morgan Stanley to fund the project's early construction phase
key_facts.excerpt: To fund the project's early construction phase, Riot arranged a $573 million interim financing facility through Morgan Stanley as it works toward putting a permanent credit backstop in place.

key_facts.fact: The lease is Anthropic's third major compute procurement in three months, taking its commitments past $60 billion
key_facts.excerpt: For Anthropic, the deal represents its third major compute procurement in three months, totaling over $60 billion in commitments.

stories.headline: OpenAI buys back $7B in employee shares at a flat $852B valuation, using its own cash

key_facts.fact: OpenAI completed a secondary share sale of roughly $7 billion on Monday, letting current and former employees sell stock at the company's $852 billion valuation
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI completed a secondary share sale totaling roughly $7 billion, allowing current and former employees to sell stock at the company's $852 billion valuation, CNBC confirmed on Monday.

key_facts.fact: The $852 billion price is unchanged from OpenAI's record $122 billion funding round that closed in March 2026, the first flat print across its run of tenders
key_facts.excerpt: Each of those increased the number. This one didn't. $852 billion in, $852 billion out, the first flat print across OpenAI's run of tenders.

key_facts.fact: Unlike prior tenders that brought in outside buyers such as Thrive Capital and SoftBank, OpenAI funded this buyback with its own cash, according to two people familiar with the terms
key_facts.excerpt: In its last two employee tenders, OpenAI brought in outside buyers, Thrive Capital and SoftBank among them, to purchase the shares. This time, according to two people familiar with the matter, OpenAI used its own cash.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI filed its IPO prospectus confidentially with the SEC in June 2026 and has not disclosed a listing date; analysts read the tender and flat price as a sign an IPO is not imminent
key_facts.excerpt: The company also filed confidentially with the Securities and Exchange Commission in June to prepare for a potential IPO later this year. However, a tender offer suggests that an IPO may not be forthcoming soon.

key_facts.fact: Previous tenders were $6.6 billion at a $500 billion valuation in October 2025 and $1.5 billion in 2024, when OpenAI was worth $157 billion
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI ran a $6.6 billion employee sale in October 2025 at a $500 billion valuation... Before that, a smaller $1.5 billion tender to SoftBank in November 2024, when the company was worth $157 billion.

key_facts.fact: The tender was first reported by Bloomberg and confirmed by CNBC; OpenAI declined to comment
key_facts.excerpt: The $7 billion figure was first reported by Bloomberg... OpenAI submitted its IPO prospectus to the Securities and Exchange Commission under confidential cover in June without disclosing when it might actually list.

key_facts.excerpt: We're making Claude Sonnet 5's introductory pricing permanent.

key_facts.fact: The introductory price had been scheduled to run only through August 31, after which it was set to rise

key_facts.fact: Anthropic launched Sonnet 5 in June, pitching it as its most agentic Sonnet, able to make plans, use browsers and terminals and run autonomously at a level that until recently required larger, more expensive models

stories.headline: Nvidia releases Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, an open 30B agent model, plus an open model router

key_facts.fact: Nvidia released Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, an open 30-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 3 billion active parameters, built for high-volume, low-latency execution in always-on AI agents
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is a 30B parameter, open Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 3B active parameters, specifically optimized for high-volume, low-latency execution in always-on AI agents and agentic workflows.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia says Lightning delivers up to 4x faster output than comparable models in its class and completes agentic tasks roughly 30% faster than Qwen3.6-35B at matching accuracy
key_facts.excerpt: According to Nvidia, Lightning delivers up to 4x faster output than comparable models in its class, completing agentic tasks roughly 30% faster than Qwen3.6-35B at matching accuracy.

key_facts.fact: Alongside the model Nvidia released NeMo Switchyard, an open-source routing library that sends each step of an agent workflow to the most suitable model; Nvidia says the pairing holds frontier-level task completion while cutting benchmark costs to roughly a third of running Opus 4.8 alone
key_facts.excerpt: Paired through Switchyard, Nvidia says the combination holds frontier-level task completion while cutting benchmark costs to roughly a third of running Opus 4.8 alone.

key_facts.fact: Weights, training data and recipes are released under the permissive OpenMDW-1.1 license, with the model on Hugging Face, ModelScope, OpenRouter and build.nvidia.com as an NIM microservice
key_facts.excerpt: the weights, training data, and recipes are released as permissively as possible under OpenMDW-1.1... try it on build.nvidia.com or through OpenRouter. Download the weights from Hugging Face, and ModelScope.

key_facts.fact: Switchyard partners include agent frameworks Cognition, LangChain and Nous Research, and LLM gateways Kong, LiteLLM and OpenRouter, which have built support into their products
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia split its partners into two groups: agent frameworks that call Switchyard directly, including Cognition, LangChain and Nous Research, and LLM gateways that have built Switchyard support into their own products, including Kong, LiteLLM and OpenRouter.

key_facts.fact: The model extends the hybrid Mamba-Transformer latent MoE architecture Nvidia introduced with the Nemotron 3 family, and is designed for agent harnesses like OpenClaw and Hermes Agent
key_facts.excerpt: It is designed for harnesses like OpenClaw and Hermes Agent—all supported by the NVIDIA NemoClaw open source security and management stack for running always-on AI agents.

stories.headline: Nvidia enlists six Wall Street firms to mobilize over $500B for AI compute financing

key_facts.fact: Nvidia announced on August 10, 2026 strategic partnerships to establish independent compute financing platforms with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR, aiming to mobilize over $500 billion of third-party capital for AI infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA today announced strategic partnerships to establish independent compute financing platforms with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to mobilize over $500 billion of third-party capital for the buildout of AI infrastructure over time.

key_facts.fact: The deals are memorandums of understanding, not final contracts: Nvidia says the partnerships 'remain subject to execution of the final agreements.'
key_facts.excerpt: Memorandums of understanding signed with six of the world's premier financial institutions... These partnerships remain subject to execution of the final agreements.

key_facts.fact: The structure lets Nvidia customers — hyperscalers, frontier AI labs and enterprises — finance GPUs and data centers with institutional credit and private capital instead of their own balance sheets.
key_facts.excerpt: By using institutional credit, insurance funds and private capital to underwrite GPUs and data centers, Nvidia is helping its end users secure financing without tapping their own balance sheets.

key_facts.fact: BlackRock CEO Larry Fink called the project the start of the 'next future for financial engineering,' comparing it to the creation of mortgage-backed securities in the 1970s.
key_facts.excerpt: BlackRock's Fink said that he believed this project was the start of the 'next future for financial engineering,' akin to the creation of mortgage-backed securities in the 1970s.

key_facts.fact: Blackstone President Jon Gray said AI compute will be seen as a 'financeable asset class' like homes are to mortgage lenders, and that AI use at Blackstone portfolio companies has surged sevenfold this year.
key_facts.excerpt: AI compute will be seen as a 'financeable asset class' in the same way that mortgage lenders look at homes, Gray of Blackstone said on CNBC. Demand for AI is outstripping supply, with use at Blackstone portfolio companies surging sevenfold this year.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia did not disclose financial terms, individual firm commitments or a timetable for deploying the planned $500 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: The company did not disclose the financial terms, investment commitments by individual firms or a timetable for deploying the planned $500 billion.

stories.headline: IBM signs $240M deal to build Together AI an Nvidia B300 inference cluster on IBM Cloud

key_facts.fact: IBM announced on August 11, 2026 a multi-year $240 million agreement with Together AI to deploy a large cluster of Nvidia HGX B300 systems on IBM Cloud, with availability expected in Q1 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Under a multi-year $240M agreement between IBM and Together AI, IBM is positioned to deploy a large cluster of NVIDIA HGX B300 systems on IBM Cloud with expected availability in Q1 2027.

key_facts.fact: It is the first dedicated, large-scale cluster built for inference on IBM Cloud, using HGX B300 systems with Nvidia Spectrum-X Ethernet networking; Nvidia says the combination delivers 30x more AI factory output than prior generations.
key_facts.excerpt: This deployment is the first dedicated, large-scale cluster built for inference on IBM Cloud using HGX B300 systems and NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet networking. According to NVIDIA, it is built to deliver 30x more AI factory output compared to prior generations.

key_facts.fact: Together AI will use the cluster to serve open-source model inference to enterprise customers; its platform now processes about 400 trillion tokens a month.
key_facts.excerpt: The neocloud plans to use IBM's Cloud capacity to support its open-source AI model inference business for enterprise customers. Together AI says its platform now processes about 400 trillion tokens a month.

key_facts.fact: The deal pushes IBM into the neocloud market by making Together AI a major cloud tenant rather than a competitor, extending an IBM-Nvidia partnership announced in March to bring Blackwell Ultra GPUs to IBM Cloud.
key_facts.excerpt: The agreement gives IBM a foothold in that market by making Together AI a major cloud tenant rather than a direct competitor... The companies announced plans in March to bring Nvidia Blackwell Ultra GPUs to IBM Cloud.

key_facts.fact: Together AI said it chose IBM and Nvidia for their product roadmaps and the speed of GPU capacity delivery at the lowest possible token cost.

stories.headline: Oil settles 5% higher as Trump and Iran trade war-compensation demands over Hormuz

key_facts.fact: Brent crude futures settled up $4.17, or 4.99%, at $87.72 a barrel on Aug. 10, while US West Texas Intermediate closed $3.95, or 5.05%, higher at $82.13 — the biggest percentage gains for both benchmarks since July 29.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude futures settled up $4.17, or 4.99%, at $87.72 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures closed $3.95, or 5.05%, at $82.13. The percentage gains were the highest since July 29 on both contracts.

key_facts.fact: The jump reversed last week's slide, when both benchmarks fell more than 7% on hopes Iran and Oman were near a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which carried a fifth of the world's oil and LNG before the conflict began in late February.
key_facts.excerpt: Both benchmarks fell more than 7% last week on hopes that Iran and Oman were close to reaching a deal that would result in a reopening of the strait, which carried a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas before the start of the Middle East conflict in late February.

key_facts.fact: President Donald Trump said Iran must pay compensation for "all of the people that they have killed and gravely wounded," countering Tehran's own demand for war reparations, an end to sanctions and the lifting of the US naval blockade before Hormuz reopens.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran also said the U.S. must lift sanctions on Tehran, and meet a number of other conditions for reopening the vital waterway, while U.S. President Donald Trump said Iran must pay compensation for "all of the people that they have killed and gravely wounded."

key_facts.fact: US Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude stocks fell by about 6.1 million barrels last week to 298.7 million barrels, the lowest level since January 1983, according to Department of Energy data.
key_facts.excerpt: On the U.S. supply side, stocks of crude oil in the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell by about 6.1 million barrels to 298.7 million barrels last week, the lowest level since January 1983, according to data from the Department of Energy.

key_facts.fact: Consultancy Energy Aspects said on Aug. 10 that an average of only five vessels a day are transiting Hormuz, down from 14 a day after the June US-Iran memorandum of understanding, and Houthi militants claimed an attack on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery a day earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: Energy Aspects said on Monday that only an average of five vessels are transiting through the strait, far below the 14 ships a day seen after the US and Iran reached a memorandum of understanding in June.

key_facts.fact: Brent was up about 16% versus pre-war levels, with shipping through the strait collapsing to between eight and 15 vessels a day in early August against roughly 130 transits before the conflict.
key_facts.excerpt: Between eight and 15 vessels crossed the strait on August 4, August 5 and August 6, according to ship-tracking platform MarineTraffic, a fraction of the roughly 130 transits before the conflict.

stories.headline: Archer Aviation to buy Boeing's Wisk, Insitu and SkyGrid; Boeing takes ~20% stake

key_facts.fact: Boeing and Archer Aviation announced on Aug. 10 that they signed definitive agreements for Archer to acquire Boeing's Wisk Aero (autonomous eVTOL), SkyGrid (airspace management software) and Insitu (military drones) subsidiaries.
key_facts.excerpt: The Boeing Company (NYSE: BA) and Archer Aviation Inc. (NYSE: ACHR) today announced the companies have signed definitive agreements in which Archer will acquire Boeing's Wisk Aero, SkyGrid and Insitu subsidiaries.

key_facts.fact: Insitu is a profitable defense business generating more than $200 million in annual revenue with operations across 35 countries; it has built more than 3,500 unmanned aircraft systems and is based in Bingen, Washington.
key_facts.excerpt: Insitu, based in Bingen, Klickitat County, and part of Boeing's defense business, has offices in the U.S., Australia, the UK and the UAE. It has manufactured more than 3,500 unmanned aircraft systems and generates $200 million in annual revenue, according to the news release published Monday.

key_facts.fact: The all-stock deal makes Boeing the largest outside shareholder in Archer with a near-20% stake; Boeing also agreed to invest up to $55 million in an upcoming Archer funding round, receives warrants for up to $200 million of stock and the right to nominate a board director.
key_facts.excerpt: Boeing has also agreed to invest up to $55 million in an upcoming Archer funding round and will receive warrants to purchase up to $200 million of the company's stock in the future.

key_facts.fact: Boeing keeps access to Wisk's core autonomous flight technology for current and next-generation commercial and defense aircraft through a technology-sharing arrangement, while Archer says the combination creates an "end-to-end physical AI platform" alongside its ZEE aerospace foundation model.
key_facts.excerpt: Combines Wisk, SkyGrid and Insitu's pioneering autonomy and airspace intelligence software with Archer's leading purpose-built AI foundation model for aerospace and defense, ZEE.

key_facts.fact: Archer shares jumped about 20% to $6.69 on Aug. 10 while peers Joby (+2%) and EHang (-1%) barely moved and Boeing was roughly flat; Archer had entered the session down 26% year to date.
key_facts.excerpt: Archer Aviation (NYSE:ACHR) stock is surging 20% to $6.69 Monday morning after the eVTOL developer announced a landmark transaction with Boeing (NYSE:BA).

key_facts.fact: In Q2 results released the same day, Archer posted $5 million in revenue against a $263.2 million net loss and $1.56 billion in liquidity; Insitu alone would add more than the company's entire quarterly revenue once the deal closes by year-end, pending Hart-Scott-Rodino antitrust review.
key_facts.excerpt: That transaction, expected to close by year-end, would add more than $200 million in annual revenue from Insitu alone, a figure that dwarfs Archer's entire reported quarterly revenue of $5 million... The net loss widened to $263.2 million from $217.7 million the prior quarter... Archer ended the period with $1.56 billion in liquidity.

stories.headline: Brazil's inflation slows to 0.07% in July, pulling the 12-month rate back under the 4.5% ceiling

key_facts.fact: IBGE reported on Aug. 11 that the IPCA rose 0.07% in July, down from 0.16% in June — the lowest July reading since 2022.
key_facts.excerpt: A inflação oficial do Brasil, medida pelo IPCA... desacelerou a 0,07% em julho, após marcar 0,16% em junho... A taxa de 0,07% é a menor para meses de julho em quatro anos, desde 2022.

key_facts.fact: The 12-month rate fell to 4.44% from 4.64%, back below the 4.5% upper bound of the central bank's tolerance band, after breaching the ceiling in May; the year-to-date increase is 3.44%.
key_facts.excerpt: No acumulado do ano, a inflação chega a 3,44%. Em 12 meses, o índice ficou em 4,44%, abaixo dos 4,64% registrados nos 12 meses anteriores e também do teto da meta de inflação, de 4,5%.

key_facts.fact: Housing was the biggest upward contributor, rising 0.99% as residential electricity accelerated to 3.09% in July from 1.53% in June.
key_facts.excerpt: O grupo Habitação teve a maior alta e o principal impacto sobre o índice, com avanço de 0,99% e contribuição de 0,15 ponto percentual. O resultado foi puxado principalmente pela energia elétrica residencial, que acelerou de 1,53% em junho para 3,09% em julho.

key_facts.fact: Food and beverages fell 0.67%, with tomatoes down 29.09%, potatoes down 19.59% and carrots down 14.41%.
key_facts.excerpt: Já o grupo Alimentação e Bebidas registrou queda de 0,67%... O tomate ficou 29,09% mais barato, a batata recuou 19,59% e a cenoura teve queda de 14,41%.

key_facts.fact: It was the fourth consecutive month of deceleration and the lowest monthly print since August 2025 (0.11%), matching the 0.07% median in the central bank's Focus survey published Aug. 10, which still sees 5.02% inflation for full-year 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: O boletim Focus desta segunda-feira (10)... projetava que a inflação de julho ficaria em 0,07%. Para o fim de 2026, o mercado espera IPCA em 5,02%... O resultado de julho foi o menor desde agosto de 2025, quando o IPCA marcou 0,11%.

stories.headline: Singapore lifts 2026 growth forecast to 4.5%-5.5%, crediting the global AI capex boom

key_facts.fact: Singapore's Ministry of Trade and Industry said on Aug. 11 that it expects GDP to grow 4.5% to 5.5% in 2026, sharply above its earlier 2% to 4% forecast.
key_facts.excerpt: The Ministry of Trade and Industry expects Singapore's economy to expand by 4.5 per cent to 5.5 per cent in 2026, sharply higher than the earlier forecast of 2 per cent to 4 per cent.

key_facts.fact: MTI permanent secretary Beh Swan Gin said at an Aug. 11 briefing that the global AI investment boom has been stronger than expected since the May forecast, providing significant tailwinds for AI-related production and exports.
key_facts.excerpt: Beh Swan Gin, permanent secretary at the Ministry of Trade and Industry, said at a virtual media briefing on Aug 11 that since the previous forecast in May, the global artificial intelligence investment boom has been stronger than expected.

key_facts.fact: It is the second upgrade to the outlook, which was set at 2%-4% in February before the outbreak of the war in Iran and originally at 1%-3% last year.
key_facts.excerpt: Gross domestic product is expected to come in at 4.5%-5.5% this year, the Ministry of Trade and Industry said on Tuesday, raising the 2%-4% estimate it set back in February before the outbreak of the war in Iran. It's the second upward revision to the growth outlook, which was initially set at 1%-3% last year.

key_facts.fact: Final second-quarter GDP came in at 5.9% year on year, above the 5.7% advance estimate, with manufacturing accelerating to 12.5% growth and first-half growth at 6.1%.
key_facts.excerpt: Singapore's economy grew by 5.9% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026... Goods-producing industries expanded 10.5% (vs 7.9% in Q1), as manufacturing growth accelerated to 12.5% from 7.3%... bringing first-half growth to 6.1%.

key_facts.fact: Key exports rose 27.4% in the second quarter on AI-driven demand for semiconductors and electronics, helping offset the drag from the Iran war and US tariffs.
key_facts.excerpt: Demand for semiconductors and electronic devices needed to power AI workloads at data centres worldwide has boomed in 2026, helping economies across Asia, including Singapore, mitigate the negative impacts of the Iran war and US trade tariffs.

key_facts.fact: Private economists moved with the government: Maybank raised its 2026 forecast to 5.2% from 4.8% and UOB to 5%, while RHB held at 4.5% citing remaining risks.
key_facts.excerpt: Maybank economists Chua Hak Bin and Brian Lee upgraded their 2026 GDP growth forecasts to 5.2 per cent from 4.8 per cent... UOB associate economist Jester Koh also upgraded his 2026 GDP growth forecast to 5 per cent from 4.8 per cent previously.

stories.headline: Australia's central bank holds rates at 4.35% and keeps a tightening bias on oil-driven inflation

key_facts.fact: The Reserve Bank of Australia's Monetary Policy Board left the cash rate target unchanged at 4.35% on Aug. 11, after three increases earlier in 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: At its meeting today, the Board decided to leave the cash rate target unchanged at 4.35 per cent.

key_facts.fact: The board said inflation is "still too high" and is not expected to return to around the 2.5% midpoint of the target range until late 2027, warning it would raise rates further if upside risks materialise.
key_facts.excerpt: It is not expected to return to around the midpoint of the target range until late 2027 and there are upside risks to this projection... including increasing the cash rate target further if upside risks materialise.

key_facts.fact: The RBA cut its December headline inflation forecast to 3.6% from 4% and trimmed mean to 3.3% from 3.5%, after the oil shock from the Middle East conflict passed through less than feared; the decision was unanimous, reversing May's 8-1 split.
key_facts.excerpt: The RBA lowered its forecast for headline inflation to 3.6% by December, compared with its previous estimate of 4%... Its forecast for trimmed mean inflation... was also reduced to 3.3% from 3.5%. The decision was unanimous.

key_facts.fact: The bank said global oil supply will take time to recover and that higher fuel prices are being passed through to other goods and services, adding directly to inflation on top of domestic capacity pressures.
key_facts.excerpt: The disruption to global oil supply is adding directly to inflation and there are indications that higher fuel prices are being passed through to prices of other goods and services, so inflation is likely to remain high for some time.

key_facts.fact: The RBA noted that growth in Australia's major trading partners has been stronger than expected because the boost from AI-related investment has outweighed the adverse effects of the Middle East conflict.
key_facts.excerpt: So far, growth in Australias major trading partners has been stronger than expected, as the boost from AI-related investment has outweighed the adverse effects of the Middle East conflict.

stories.headline: MoonLake's nanobody sonelokimab hits every endpoint in Phase 3 psoriatic arthritis trial

key_facts.fact: MoonLake Immunotherapeutics said on Aug. 10 that the Phase 3 IZAR-1 trial of sonelokimab met all clinical endpoints at week 16 in biologic-naive adults with active psoriatic arthritis.
key_facts.excerpt: Phase 3 IZAR-1 trial in bio-naïve patients met all clinical endpoints at Week 16 for 60 mg sonelokimab

key_facts.fact: The primary endpoint was met with 42.1% of patients on 60 mg sonelokimab with induction achieving an ACR50 response, while 66.5% achieved ACR20, 41.2% reached minimal disease activity and 61% of those with skin involvement hit PASI90.
key_facts.excerpt: A total of 42.1% of biologic-naïve patients treated with sonelokimab 60 mg with induction achieved an ACR50 response... 66.5% of patients achieved ACR20, and 41.2% achieved MDA at Week 16. In patients with concomitant skin involvement, 61% achieved PASI90 at Week 16.

key_facts.fact: Under an unblinding protocol agreed with the FDA, only absolute response rates for the 60 mg arm were released; comparisons versus placebo stay blinded until the Phase 3 program completes, and the blinded safety analysis showed no new safety signals.
key_facts.excerpt: Consistent with the unblinding protocol defined with the FDA, topline disclosure at Week 16 includes absolute response levels and endpoint outcomes for the sonelokimab 60 mg with induction arm... The blinded safety analysis of IZAR-1 suggests a profile consistent with previous clinical studies and no new safety signals were observed.

key_facts.fact: IZAR-1 and IZAR-2 together enroll roughly 1,500 adults; IZAR-2 tests TNF-refractory patients against AbbVie's Skyrizi (risankizumab) and is expected to finish enrollment in Q3 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The second trial, Izar-2, is being conducted in patients who have not seen improvement in symptoms after taking TNF inhibitors such as AbbVie's Humira, and it will directly compare sonelokimab with AbbVie's Skyrizi.

key_facts.fact: Alongside the data, MoonLake reported $537.0 million in cash and short-term securities at the end of Q2, a runway to mid-2028, and said it expects to file a Biologics License Application by the end of September 2026 for its lead indication.
key_facts.excerpt: MoonLake ended the second quarter with $537.0 million in cash, cash equivalents and short-term marketable debt securities and expects to have a cash runway to mid-2028... End September 2026: Expected submission of Biologics License Application (BLA).

stories.headline: US appeals court lets thousands of youth-addiction suits against Meta, TikTok and Google proceed

key_facts.fact: The 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals ruled on Aug. 10 that Meta, Alphabet's Google, ByteDance's TikTok and Snap must face more than 3,000 federal lawsuits alleging they designed their platforms to be addictive to young users.
key_facts.excerpt: The San Francisco-based 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals rejected the companies' bid to reverse a lower court's ruling forcing them to face more than 3,000 lawsuits over the claims filed in federal court, concluding that the appeal came too early in the litigation.

key_facts.fact: The panel held that Section 230 of the 1996 Communications Decency Act provides a defense to liability, not immunity from being sued, making the companies' interlocutory appeal premature; Circuit Judge Jacqueline Nguyen wrote that Meta's implied-immunity argument fails.
key_facts.excerpt: "Although Section 230 does not expressly provide for immunity from suit, Meta argues that such immunity should be implied. We disagree," Circuit Judge Jacqueline Hong-Ngoc Nguyen wrote in her opinion.

key_facts.fact: The court also denied Meta's bid to postpone a trial brought by 29 state attorneys general alleging the company illegally collected children's data, designed platforms to keep young users hooked and misled consumers about safety.
key_facts.excerpt: The court also denied Meta's bid to postpone a trial beginning Wednesday in a lawsuit brought by 29 state attorneys general alleging that the company illegally collected and used children's data, designed their social media platforms to keep young users hooked, and misled consumers about their safety.

key_facts.fact: The federal cases — filed by states, municipalities, school districts and individuals — are centralized before US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers in Oakland; roughly 3,300 more are consolidated in California state court.
key_facts.excerpt: The cases, which have been centralized before U.S. District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers in Oakland, California, seek damages, penalties and restitution from the companies... with approximately 3,300 of them in a consolidated proceeding in California state court.

key_facts.fact: The ruling adds to a string of losses: a Los Angeles jury in March found Meta and Google negligent and awarded $6 million to a 20-year-old plaintiff, and a New Mexico jury ordered Meta to pay $375 million, with a judge last week adding $567 million for creating a public nuisance.
key_facts.excerpt: A Los Angeles jury in March found Meta and Google negligent for designing social media platforms that harm young people. The jury awarded $6 million... A jury in March ordered it to pay $375 million after finding it had misled consumers about the safety of its platforms. On Thursday, a judge found Meta had created a public nuisance and ordered it to pay an additional $567 million.
